title: Tamsin and the Colony
premise: Rafael Ashgrove, an insurance investigator exiled to the forgotten colony of Tamsin's Landing, documents its slow decay while hiding a past that made him a target of the Meridian Combine. When a deep-space vessel returns with its crew aged backward and memories intact, Rafael realizes the colony was never abandoned—it was a decades-long experiment in memory erasure, and he is its last unaltered witness. Pursued by Combine retrievers who want his records destroyed, he races across dying settlements toward a dead-space relay to broadcast the truth before the signal window closes. He reaches it, but broadcasting means revealing his own erased crimes alongside the Combine's; he sends everything, choosing truth over the loyalty of the colonists who sheltered him, and dies as the signal escapes.
about_author: Casper Reyes is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent eleven years investigating losses no one wanted to pay for. They write slow-burn science fiction about paperwork, grief, and the people history files under 'acceptable loss.'

chapters.title: The Actuary of Small Disasters
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael arrives at Tamsin's Landing to close out a policy on a collapsed water reclaimer, cataloguing a colony everyone else has written off. Through dry field reports we meet innkeeper Sefa Oduya and the town's quiet dignity. Emotional beat: weary professional detachment beginning to crack into reluctant affection.

chapters.title: A Ledger of Vanishing Names
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Investigating a 'misfiled' death, Rafael finds colonial registry records that contradict themselves—residents listed as departed who never left. Sefa warns him to stop asking. Flashbacks hint at why Rafael was assigned somewhere so remote. Emotional beat: unease; the sense of being watched by an absence.

chapters.title: The Ship That Came Home Younger
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. The long-lost survey vessel Perihelion returns after forty years with a crew biologically aged backward, memories intact but bodies wrong. One crew member, Ilsa Vann, recognizes Rafael's face from a file she shouldn't remember. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What the Combine Erases
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Vann. Ilsa's chapter: she recalls the deep-space relay her ship passed, and the Combine facility that 'processed' them before return. She tells Rafael the colony itself is a control group for selective memory excision—and that unaltered witnesses are retrieved, not interviewed. Emotional beat: guilt and resolve.

chapters.title: Retrieval Notice
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. A Combine retrieval team lands under cover of a 'medical charter.' Rafael's hidden archive—the decade of reports he's secretly compiled—is compromised when a local informant sells him out. Sefa hides him anyway, knowing the cost. Emotional beat: betrayal by proximity; loyalty offered without conditions.

chapters.title: The Long Road Through Dead Country
chapters.summary: POV Rafael, with Ilsa. Fleeing overland toward the edge-of-dead-space relay, they cross settlements already half-erased—towns whose residents can't remember their own children's names. Rafael confesses fragments of his own buried crime to Ilsa. Emotional beat: the road as confession; trust built in motion.

chapters.title: Signal Window
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. At a derelict waystation they learn the relay only accepts broadcasts during a narrow alignment window—eleven days away, and the retrievers are two days behind them. Ilsa discovers Rafael's full file: what he did before exile, and who he covered for. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against truth; she chooses to keep walking beside him.

chapters.title: The Price of the Record
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Ambushed at the relay's approach, Rafael bargains with the retriever commander—a former colleague who offers to restore his erased life if he surrenders the archive. Rafael sees the trap: restoration means accepting the Combine's version of himself. Emotional beat: temptation of a clean identity versus a guilty true one.

chapters.title: Everything, Unredacted
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. During the alignment window, wounded and cornered in the relay core, Rafael uploads the entire archive—his crimes included—unredacted. The retrievers cut power mid-transmission; Sefa, arriving with colonial volunteers, holds the ground long enough for the final packet to clear. Emotional beat: climax—truth chosen at lethal cost.

chapters.title: Tamsin and the Colony
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Weeks later, the signal reaches the outer systems; inquiries begin. Sefa reads Rafael's final report, which names every colonist with precision and tenderness, and buries him beneath the repaired reclaimer where he first worked. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into record—the colony remembered because he refused to forget it.
